codex.text: Two free parameters (10-bar window, 20th/80th bounds) are asserted without justification or sensitivity analysis, and any iteration after touching the holdout—re-tuning percentiles and re-testing—burns the seal, turning your "validation" into selection on the test set. "Improve" is unmeasurable as stated: no minimum effect size, no significance test, and no accounting for the reduced sample size when the filter drops trades—a profit-factor delta on 30 filtered trades is noise. Reusing "the same sealed holdout" across repeated challenger evaluations means it is no longer sealed; you need fresh untouched data or nested walk-forward before holdout contact. Finally, "accept it for further consideration" is governance-vague—if that path bypasses the full `promote.py` gate chain, this proposal is structurally unsafe regardless of its numbers.

opencode.text: The proposal risks severe selection and lookahead bias by deriving `validated_states.json` from the same survivor strategies and `validated_opportunities` whose unusually strong metrics motivate the test. “Fill-rate improves” lacks a predefined threshold, sample size, time horizon, cost model, and out-of-sample or sealed-holdout comparison; moreover, testing only whether expectancy turns negative is far too weak to establish benefit. It also omits registry requirements, baseline tests, leakage checks, and explicit confirmation that only research artifacts—not protected live YAML or runtime gating—will be modified.

decision.rationale: REAL: falsifiable candidate registered as challenger council_the-aegis-mt5-demo-bot-is-running-the-in_249619 for the validation pipeline

proposals.text: In the next research cycle, execute the ml_pipeline to populate `validated_states.json` from the survivor strategies underlying the current `validated_opportunities` (GBPUSD trend/asia/buy, expectancy_validate=1.824, PF_validate=3.027, win_rate_validate=72.7%). Measure firehose fill‑rate and net expectancy with the validated‑state gate active versus the current all‑blocked state. Falsify if fill‑rate does not improve or net expectancy turns negative, indicating the gate without populated states degrades economics. If supported, incrementally expand the allowlist from subsequent survivor strategies in following cycles.

Test a challenger that adds a 10-bar realized-volatility regime filter, permitting existing validated-state entries only when volatility is between the instrument’s rolling 20th and 80th percentiles. Register the experiment and evaluate it on the same sealed holdout with identical spread/slippage assumptions. Accept it for further consideration only if net expectancy and profit factor improve while maximum drawdown does not worsen; otherwise reject and retain the current champion unchanged.

question: The AEGIS MT5 DEMO bot is running the intelligent firehose with the validated-state gate. Given the current measured evidence, identify ONE concrete, falsifiable improvement candidate for the next research cycle. Do not modify code or the champion. Cite book corpus passages if relevant.

codex.text: Pre-register the 10-bar realized-volatility window and 20th/80th-percentile bounds from training data and test a fixed sensitivity grid exclusively through nested walk-forward analysis, selecting the challenger before any sealed-holdout contact. Evaluate the frozen challenger once on fresh untouched holdout data under identical spread/slippage assumptions, with minimum trade-count and coverage thresholds, predefined economically meaningful improvements in net expectancy and profit factor, a non-inferiority margin for maximum drawdown, and uncertainty assessed by an appropriate bootstrap test. Register every specification, selection step, result, and failure in `ExperimentRegistry`; after holdout exposure, prohibit parameter iteration unless a new untouched holdout is reserved. Promotion may occur only through the complete `promote.py` gate chain and its authorized promotion script; otherwise retain the current champion and archive the challenger and holdout result.

opencode.text: Revised proposal: In the next research cycle, first register the experiment via `ExperimentRegistry` and confirm the baseline pytest suite stays green, then run ml_pipeline to populate `validated_states.json` from an earlier, pre-registered survivor cohort—not the same strategies whose metrics motivate the test—with per-feature timestamp audits ruling out label leakage before any evaluation. Evaluate firehose fill-rate and net expectancy (net of the runner's spread/slippage assumptions) against the current all-blocked baseline on a sealed holdout window of ≥300 signals spanning ≥8 weeks, with success predefined as fill-rate improving by ≥10 percentage points AND net expectancy > 0 with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero. Falsify—and keep the challenger unpromoted—if any leakage audit trips, either threshold is missed, or holdout expectancy decays more than a preregistered bound relative to in-sample. All writes remain confined to research artifacts (`bot/research/`, `bot/reports/research/`, staged `validated_states.json`); protected live YAML, runtime gating, and `intel/intelligent_champion.json` are untouched, with any promotion still gated by `promote.py`. If supported, expand the allowlist one cohort per subsequent cycle, each re-tested against fresh sealed data under these same gates.
